a:r.a:t: HTTP, or Hypertext Transfer Protocol, is the foundation of data communication on the World Wide Web. It's an application layer protocol that enables the transfer of hypertext, such as HTML. HTTP defines how messages are formatted and transmitted and how web servers and browsers should respond to various commands. It operates over a client-server model, where a client (like a web browser) sends requests to a server, and the server responds with the requested information. HTTP is the basis for most data communication on the internet, facilitating the retrieval and display of web pages.
